scenes.description: Elizabeth is lying in bed, groggy and in pain from a hangover and menstrual cramps. Jisoo, her supportive friend, is trying to convince her to stay home. Meanwhile, Professor Lao sends a reminder about class attendance, increasing Elizabeth's anxiety.

scenes.plot: Elizabeth is caught between her health and academic obligations. Jisoo encourages her to rest, while Professor Lao's strictness adds pressure to attend. Elizabeth must decide whether to prioritize her well-being or risk further academic consequences.
scenes.social_purpose: To explore the tension between academic responsibility and personal health, while highlighting the role of friendship in difficult decision-making.

chunk.text: Elizabeth lies in bed, staring at the ceiling. Her body aches, and the pounding in her head reminds her of the previous night's party. Jisoo sits beside her, gently placing a hand on her shoulder. 'Elizabeth, I know you're not feeling well. Please, just rest today.' Elizabeth sighs, glancing at the clock. 'But I don't want to miss class again. Professor Lao already warned me about my absences.' Jisoo nods. 'He can't control what happens when you're sick. Take care of yourself first.' Elizabeth pulls out her phone and reads a message from Professor Lao. 'He says he's not going to tolerate any more unexcused absences. I'm already behind in the readings.' Jisoo suggests, 'Maybe you can send him a message and explain your situation. He might be more understanding if you're honest.' At that moment, a knock is heard at the door. Professor Lao enters with a clipboard in hand. 'Ms. Palmer, I see you haven't arrived for class yet. You have three absences already. I hope this isn't becoming a pattern.' Elizabeth struggles to sit up. 'I'm sorry, Professor. I'm not feeling well. I'll try to make it up somehow.' Professor Lao nods but remains firm. 'I expect you to take this seriously. Your health is important, but so is your responsibility as a student.'
